# 4.6 LCA via binary lifting

Phase 4 (Graphs), target rating 1600–2000. Bank status: not started.

## Patterns

### k-th ancestor (`kth-ancestor`)

Jump k levels up in O(log n) using ancestors at distances that are powers of two.

**Works because:** The 2^(j+1)-th ancestor is the 2^j-th ancestor of the 2^j-th ancestor.

### Lowest common ancestor queries (`lca-query`)

For many pairs, find the deepest vertex that is an ancestor of both.

**Works because:** After lifting the deeper vertex to the same depth, "ancestors differ" is monotone in the jump length.

### Distances in a tree (`path-length`)

dist(u, v) = depth(u) + depth(v) − 2 · depth(lca(u, v)), with weighted depths if edges have weights.

**Works because:** There is exactly one path between two vertices of a tree, and it passes through their lowest common ancestor.

### Minimum or maximum on a path (`path-aggregate`)

Store, with each power-of-two jump, the aggregate of the edges it covers, and combine jumps along a path.

**Works because:** The aggregate is associative (minimum, maximum, sum), so it combines over consecutive jumps.

### Adding along paths (`path-updates`)

Add a value on many u–v paths using +1 at u and v and −1 at the meeting vertex and its parent, then sum over subtrees.

**Works because:** All updates come before all reads, and a subtree sum counts exactly the paths through each vertex.
